title: Cold rebuild: Parse ss -tlnp
summary: Rebuild Parse ss -tlnp from memory, no hints.

steps.title: Cold rebuild
body: Time to prove a piece stuck. You built **Parse ss -tlnp** in *Probing the network*. Now write it again from an
**empty editor**: no starter, no hints, no solution to peek at. The tests are exactly the ones you passed
Why: pulling something out of memory is what makes it stay there. Reading your old code feels like knowing
it; rebuilding it cold shows whether you do. If you get stuck, that is useful news: go back to the lesson,
then come back and try again tomorrow.
This check, plus the boss, is what proves the module.

steps.prompt: From your laptop, `curl http://10.0.0.5:5000` says *Connection refused*. On the server, `curl localhost:5000` works and `ss -tlnp` shows `127.0.0.1:5000 dotnet`. What's wrong?
options: The app listens only on loopback; bind it to 0.0.0.0 (e.g. `ASPNETCORE_URLS=http://0.0.0.0:5000`) or put a reverse proxy in front
steps.explain: Refused (not a timeout) means the host answered but nothing listens on that address:port. A timeout would point to a firewall.

steps.title: Rebuild Parse ss -tlnp cold
prompt: Write `List<(string Address, int Port, string Process)> Listening(List<string> ss)` over `ss -tlnp` output (header line first, columns separated by runs of spaces). For each `LISTEN` line take the local address and port (split at the **last** `:` so IPv6 like `[::]:443` works) and the process name inside `users:(("..."`. Missing process column → empty string.
**From memory this time:** the editor starts empty and the tests are the ones you passed in the lesson.
Type the shape yourself, then fill it in:
List<(string Address, int Port, string Process)> Listening(List<string> ss)
